title: Noctune Free
description: Turn your own objects and lights into music visuals. Start in three steps; open advanced tips only when you need them.

sections.title: Install Noctune
sections.summary: Install one ZIP, then open the Noctune sidebar.
sections.body:
1. Use Blender 5.2 or newer. Keep your Noctune extension ZIP zipped.
  2. Open Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions. From the menu at the top right, choose Install from Disk and select the ZIP.
  3. In the 3D Viewport, press N and open the Noctune tab.

Use your own scene and objects. Noctune works locally, without an account or license-key service, in EEVEE and Cycles.

Updating an existing installation

Save your project, stop playback, and install the newer ZIP through Blender's extension manager. Keep only one Noctune edition installed at a time. Projects and looks from the former Afterglow name remain compatible.

sections.title: Your first music reaction
sections.summary: Select objects. Load music. Build. That is the everyday workflow.
sections.body:
The panel has three views: Setup to build, Style to tune the selected object, and Presets to browse looks. Music and Start Frame stay at the top.

  1. Music → Track. Use the folder icon to load your music.
  2. Setup → Objects → Use Selected. Select meshes, curves, text or lights, then press the full-width button. Missing emission is prepared on geometry.
  3. Setup → Build Reaction. Use Material Preview or Rendered shading for geometry; use Rendered for native lights. Press Space to preview.

Build Reaction calibrates the response and prepares playback while keeping your materials and appearance. A successful build opens Style. Choose a reacting object to tune it, or use Presets → Object Look → Apply Look only if you want a preset. After music changes, use Update Reaction; it keeps your styling.

Which audio files can I use?

The file picker accepts WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A and AAC. Decoding depends on your Blender installation; if a track will not load, convert it to a standard WAV file.

Keep the source audio available, or pack the sound into the project before moving it to another computer.

sections.title: Use your objects and lights
sections.summary: Ordinary materials work. Lights need no materials.
sections.body:
Use Selected accepts meshes, curves, text, and Point, Spot, Area and Sun lights. Geometry reacts through emission; native lights react through their power and color.

Missing materials receive emission-ready materials. Existing non-emissive materials use prepared copies that preserve their shader connections and textures. Original material assignments are kept for cleanup.

Collections, shared data and linked objects
  • The Setup → Objects → Collection picker can use an existing collection. Geometry chosen this way needs editable emission already; use Use Selected to prepare ordinary materials.
  • Shared materials and geometry are isolated where needed so unselected objects keep their appearance.
  • Reacting lights use their own light-data copy. Their type, aim, size and transforms stay under your control.
  • Make library-linked objects local before adding a reaction.

sections.title: Choose a look
sections.summary: Browse visual previews, then explicitly apply the look you want.
sections.body:
Build your reaction first. In Presets, open the thumbnail chooser, select an optional Object Look and press Apply Look. Applying it opens Style for further adjustments. Browsing a look does not apply it. Build and Update never apply a look.

LookFeel
Neon ClubCyan and pink, with a punchy response.
Cinematic PulseCool blue and warm gold, with a slower fade.
Aurora FlowMint and violet, with a soft response.
Signal GridIcy cyan and amber, with a crisp response.
Electric VioletViolet and neon green, with a quick pulse.

For your own palette, open Style. Change Color A, Color B and Intensity. Save the result under My Object Looks.

Build/Update Reaction keeps your current appearance and recalibrates the audio response. Only an explicit Apply Look or saved-look action changes your style.

Built-in looks preserve the colors and textures of existing emissive materials. Their palette applies to newly prepared materials and lights. To tint an existing material yourself, enable Use Colors. Built-in looks use zero Idle Glow, so emission stops during silence after the response fades. Calibration adjusts sensitivity; a manually raised Idle Glow stays on. Reflective surfaces can still be visible under scene lighting.

sections.title: Send a wave through your scene
sections.summary: Ripple makes the reaction travel instead of firing everywhere together.
sections.body:
1. Build an object reaction first.
  2. Open Style → Ripple Motion and enable it.
  3. Choose From and set Beats per Sweep. Fewer beats make the wave cross faster.

Enable Through Objects to send the wave across geometry surfaces, rather than lighting each object all at once. Keep Fast Playback enabled for this mode.

Directions, origins and moving objects
ControlUse it for
Longest Axis / X / Y / ZA sweep along the scene's longest spread or a chosen world axis.
Empty + OriginA wave spreading outward from your chosen object.
Collection CenterA wave spreading outward from the collection's middle.
Reverse arrowReverse the sweep, or make an outward wave travel inward.
Spread BandsRefresh frequency distribution and wave placement after moving objects or the Origin.

Ripple follows the detected music tempo. Native lights join the wave at their object origins; they do not have surface travel. Level Meter fill is disabled while Through Objects is on.

sections.title: Make equalizer-style objects
sections.summary: Fill geometry by loudness with Level Meter.
sections.body:
1. Select a reacting mesh, curve or text object.
  2. Open Style and enable Level Meter.
  3. Choose X, Y or Z for the object's local fill direction. Use the arrow button to invert the fill.

Use several tall objects for equalizer bars. Turn off Through Objects when you want Level Meter fill. Meter controls apply to geometry, not native lights.

sections.title: Tweak only what you need
sections.summary: Start with Intensity, Glow and the two colors. Everything else is optional.
sections.body:
Choose Style, then select a reacting object in the viewport. Its appearance controls are shown directly; expand Audio Response only when needed.

ControlSimple meaning
IntensityMake the final emission or light power brighter or dimmer.
Idle GlowKeep a little brightness during quiet sections. Set to zero for darkness between hits.
Use ColorsEnable the reaction's two-color tint.
Color A / Color BColor A is quiet; Color B is loud.
Base Power (lights)The native light's brightness scale, initially its original power.
Audio Response: frequency, response and timing

Expand Style → Audio Response for these controls.

ControlWhat it changes
Low / HighThe frequency band this object hears, in Hz. Lower bands favor bass; higher bands favor brighter sounds.
Padlock / Lock BandKeep this band when using Spread Bands.
GainIncrease the reaction's sensitivity.
ThresholdIgnore audio below this level.
DecayHow long a hit takes to fade, in seconds.
DelayMove this object's response later, in seconds.

While Ripple is enabled, the displayed Gain and Threshold control its kick response. After editing a band's limits, Decay or Delay, press Setup → Tools → Refresh Playback.

Intensity changes brightness without changing the color blend or meter fill. Final light power also depends on Base Power; Sun lights retain Blender's native Sun energy units.

sections.title: Save your own style
sections.summary: Keep looks in the project, or export them for another project.
sections.body:
1. Open Presets → My Object Looks.
  2. Enter a Name and press Save Current Look.
  3. After building, select a saved look and press Apply Only to load its style.

Export Look saves the selected snapshot as a JSON file. Import Look adds a JSON file to the library without changing the current scene.

Use Apply Only after building to load the saved style. Main Update Reaction preserves it. The optional Apply & Build shortcut explicitly performs both actions.

What gets saved?

An object look captures shared colors, Intensity, Glow and Decay from the first reacting object by name in the chosen collection. It is a style snapshot, not a copy of your scene, audio, geometry or every object's individual frequency band.

Apply Only changes styling on existing reactions. Apply & Build also builds the object reaction. The trash button removes the saved snapshot; it leaves the current scene style in place. Up to 64 saved looks can live in one project.

Object-only looks work in both Free and Pro. To send a look from current Pro to Free, export an object-only look; newer complete or environment-only Pro files are not supported by Free 0.32.1.

sections.title: Use Blender for compositor glow
sections.summary: Noctune no longer adds or edits compositor nodes.
sections.body:
Set up a glow halo directly in Blender’s compositor using its Glare / Fog Glow tools. Noctune’s compositor-glow feature and its Add/Remove Glow actions have been removed.

Object Idle Glow and Pro beam Glow still control the selected material or effect brightness; they do not change the compositor.

Updating or uninstalling an add-on does not remove nodes already saved in a .blend. If a file contains an old Noctune Render Glow node, select it in Blender’s compositor and mute it with M to bypass it. Keep your image connected to the final output.

sections.title: Timing and smooth playback
sections.summary: Build Reaction handles calibration and playback preparation for you.
sections.body:
Use Setup → Update Reaction after changing music. Apply a built-in look explicitly from Presets. It calibrates all Noctune object and light reactions in the scene and prepares playback.

Build/Update Reaction keeps your current appearance and recalibrates the audio response. Only an explicit Apply Look or saved-look action changes your style.

Set Start Frame in the shared Music card to place the music on the timeline. Use per-object Delay when one object needs a later response.

Automatic calibration

Noctune measures each frequency band over the full source track and sets its Gain and Threshold. Start Frame, Delay and Ripple placement change playback timing without changing that measurement.

Calibration normalizes the audio response; materials, light power, Intensity, Glow and scene exposure still affect the final image. If you have animated Gain or Threshold, remove their keyframes, drivers or NLA animation before automatic calibration. Your authored animation is left intact when calibration is rejected.

Setup → Tools reference

Refresh Playback and Fast Playback are directly in Tools. Expand Audio & Setup for Spread Bands, Calibrate and Refresh Reaction Setup.

ToolWhen to use it
Presets → Apply LookApply an optional Object Look to an existing reaction.
Refresh Reaction SetupRefresh reaction assignments and settings without the full automatic calibration workflow.
Spread BandsRedistribute bass-to-treble bands across unlocked objects; refresh Ripple placement.
CalibrateMeasure the track again and set response Gain and Threshold.
Fast PlaybackUse precomputed audio response for smooth geometry playback. Builds enable it automatically.
Refresh PlaybackRecompute prepared playback after changing band limits, Decay or Delay, or when the panel reports stale objects.

Lights always use prepared playback, even if Fast Playback is switched off for geometry. Noctune adds its music strip for audio-synchronized playback; Loading music, changing Start Frame, or rebuilding after an FPS change fits the timeline end to the track duration, including partial frames. An active preview range follows that end too. Later manual range edits stay until the track configuration changes again.

sections.title: Render, save and clean up
sections.summary: Compose and render with Blender; remove reactions with one cleanup action.
sections.body:
Render with Blender

  1. Set your camera and scene.
  2. In Output Properties, choose the resolution, frame range, output format and destination.
  3. Use Render → Render Animation. Set up Blender’s compositor yourself if you want a glow halo.

Noctune leaves your camera, world, render engine and output settings under your control. The timeline end follows the track duration when its music, Start Frame or frame rate changes; you can edit the range afterward.

Remove the reaction

Stop playback and expand the standalone Setup → Cleanup → Remove Object Reaction. Cleanup is in Setup, separate from styling and presets. This removes Noctune reactions and restores automatically prepared material assignments and original light data, including previous light animation.

What stays in the project?

Your geometry edits and materials or light data you reassigned manually stay in place. Saved look snapshots remain in the project. Compositor nodes remain unchanged. Bypass any old Noctune Render Glow node manually in Blender. Existing generated Pro environment effects use their own separate cleanup action.

When sharing a project, keep audio files available or pack the sound into the .blend, then save the project.

sections.title: Quick fixes
sections.summary: Start here if the result does not look right.
sections.body:
Build Reaction is disabled

Stop timeline playback. Choose Setup → Objects → Collection or use Use Selected, then load Track in Music.

Nothing glows

Switch to Material Preview or Rendered shading and move to a frame inside the song. For ordinary geometry, select it and use Use Selected before building. For native lights, use Rendered shading and make sure there are surfaces for the light to illuminate.

The reaction is too bright or stays on

Lower the selected object's Intensity or a light's Base Power. Set object Idle Glow to zero if quiet sections should go dark. Use Blender’s compositor directly if you want a halo.

The response is weak or does not follow the sound I want

Use Update Reaction to recalibrate while keeping styling. Apply a preset separately under Presets → Apply Look. To choose a specific sound range, adjust the selected object's Low / High band, lock it if needed, then Refresh Playback.

I edited settings, but playback still looks old

Use Update Reaction for a changed song. Use Apply Look for a different preset. Use Refresh Playback after band, Decay or Delay edits. Use Spread Bands after moving objects or a Ripple Origin.

Through Objects or Level Meter does not work

Through Objects needs Fast Playback. Level Meter applies to geometry and is disabled while Through Objects is enabled. Meter X/Y/Z are the object's local axes.

The halo is missing from the render

Add glow directly in Blender’s compositor; Noctune no longer provides a compositor feature. Check the final rendered image rather than only the viewport.

Audio is missing or a file will not load

Relink or reload the track with the folder icon, or use a packed sound. Convert unsupported audio to WAV. Check that the timeline is inside the music range and that Blender's sequencer audio is not muted.

Calibration or a look refuses to apply

Read the message for an animated control conflict. Keep your animation by applying the look in another scene, or remove the reported conflicting keyframes, drivers or NLA animation before applying automatic styling or calibration.

A saved Pro look will not import into Free

Ask for an object-only look. Free 0.32.1 reads the shared object-only format, but not the newest complete/environment Pro formats.

sections.title: Free and Pro
sections.summary: Free animates your objects and lights. Pro also generates the environment.
sections.body:
FeatureFreePro
Material and native-light music reactionIncludedIncluded
Five object looks, custom object looks and colorsIncludedIncluded
Ripple, Through Objects, Level Meter and soft glowIncludedIncluded
Automatic calibration and prepared playbackIncludedIncluded
Generated environment lights, beams, lasers and signalsPro featureIncluded
Environment looks, routing, placement and live layer mixPro featureIncluded

To upgrade, save your project, disable and remove Free, then install the Pro ZIP. Keep one edition installed at a time. Your existing object reactions and materials stay in the project.

Noctune was formerly called Afterglow. The internal extension ID retains that name for project compatibility. Noctune is licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later.
